issues.description: Field 'birthday' of class de.tum.in.ase.eist.model.Person has conflicting declared types across artifacts. The problem statement's UML and the template common model declare Person.birthday as java.time.LocalDate (expected by the client view), whereas the solution repository's common model declares birthday as String. The client code (PersonScene) calls person.getBirthday() and passes it to a DatePicker (DatePicker.setValue), which expects a LocalDate. This mismatch will cause compilation/type errors and confuses students which type they should implement and work with.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose and apply a single type for Person.birthday across all artifacts. Prefer changing the solution's common model (solution/src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Person.java) to declare 'private java.time.LocalDate birthday;' with corresponding getter/setter, so it matches the template, the UML in the problem statement, and the client code that uses DatePicker.setValue(LocalDate). After changing the type, update any JSON (de)serialization if necessary (e.g., configure Jackson to handle LocalDate) and run the client/server integration to ensure no further type-related errors. If instead String is intentionally required, update the problem text and all client code (PersonScene and DatePicker usage) to convert between String and LocalDate consistently — but do not leave mixed types between model and client view.
